Patient kidney sections show absent or diminished podocyte MAGI2 expression, consistent with loss of function.

nodes.description: Calcineurin inhibitors are a standard empirical option in steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, but in the magi2a zebrafish model neither cyclosporine A nor tacrolimus altered the phenotype, so efficacy specific to MAGI2 disease is not established.

The disease is steroid resistant by definition. In the magi2a zebrafish model, corticosteroid treatment paradoxically worsened the nephrotic phenotype with earlier edema onset, so steroids are not expected to help and may be harmful.

Dendrin normally localizes at the slit diaphragm; when MAGI-2 is lost, dephosphorylated dendrin accumulates in the nucleus of injured podocytes and promotes apoptosis, leading to progressive podocyte loss and glomerulosclerosis. This mechanism is established in mouse models and has not been directly demonstrated in patient tissue.

nodes.description: Kidney transplantation is the definitive treatment once kidney failure is reached. The finding that makes it the main actionable statement here is that monogenic steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome does not recur in the graft, unlike genetic-testing-negative non-responders, in whom recurrence was 73 percent. That finding is for monogenic steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome as a class, not for MAGI2 in particular; no transplanted MAGI2 patient has been reported. Establishing the molecular diagnosis is therefore what carries the prognostic information.

nodes.description: Not a treatment for this disease, and recorded as an emerging direction only. AAV-delivered MAGI2 protected podocytes from apoptosis and improved renal function, but the model was diabetic kidney disease, in which MAGI2 is acquiredly downregulated rather than mutated, and the animals carried two wild-type MAGI2 alleles. Whether restoring MAGI2 helps a patient with biallelic truncating variants is untested, and no MAGI2 gene-therapy study in a MAGI2-mutant model has been reported.

Constitutive Magi-2 null mice develop progressive proteinuria from 2 weeks of age with loss of glomerular nephrin, diffuse foot process effacement and progressive podocyte loss, and die of renal failure by 3 months.
